note: A full xdist run scheduled test_desks before unrelated memory tests on one worker. Its SerialMatcher remained process-global, normalized every nonnumeric phrase to NONE, and produced 40 false failures plus one setup error. A different collection order had hidden the leak.

decisions.question: How should tests isolate Nestor's process-wide matcher under parallel collection?
decisions.commitment: The existing isolate_globals autouse fixture now saves the current matcher, installs a fresh StringMatcher before each test, and restores the saved matcher afterward, alongside its existing store, ledger, keyring, forwarder, and environment isolation.
decisions.why: An xdist worker is a long-lived interpreter. Process globals cross module boundaries even though files and stores are temporary, so scheduling order must not decide which normalization algorithm an unrelated test receives.

decisions.question: What proves the matcher isolation resets without permanently overwriting caller state?
decisions.commitment: A regression test installs a poison matcher that maps every value to NONE, enters the fixture body and requires StringMatcher, then completes teardown and requires the exact poison object to be restored.
decisions.why: Reset-only isolation could make the suite green while damaging an embedding caller that deliberately installed a matcher around a nested test run. The fixture owns the test interval, not the process outside it.
